checkbox.name: Checkbox
checkbox.purpose: Use Checkbox for one independent boolean choice, item selection, or partial aggregate selection where the label must stay visible with checked, unchecked, indeterminate, focus, error, and disabled states.
checkbox.referenceRationale: The ZIP reference gives the visual benchmark: compact square control, clear selected accent, indeterminate support, and spring-like feedback. Design System keeps ownership of color, type, density, state, icon, motion, and accessibility rules.

anatomy.rule: Names the choice in plain language and remains visible in every state.
Owns size, radius, border, fill, and focus treatment.
Shows check or mixed state only when selected or indeterminate.
Adds optional description, validation, or policy reason without replacing the label.

variants.description: Choice with support text for policy or consequence.
Aggregate choice that can become indeterminate.
Dense row for tables, filters, and settings lists.

checkbox.statePrecedence: disabled > error > focus > indeterminate > checked > unchecked

Energy.decision: Use Energy for box fill, border, status, and disabled contrast.
Energy.behavior: Energy makes selected, mixed, error, and disabled states visible.
Energy.example: Fuel card permission rows show selected accent and clear disabled contrast.
Energy.test: Verify contrast for unchecked, checked, mixed, error, and disabled.
Energy.rejectIf: Color is raw or selection depends on color alone.

Voice.decision: Use Voice for label and support text.
Voice.behavior: Voice keeps the choice readable at each density.
Voice.example: Driver alert choices explain the operational result.
Voice.test: Verify label and support text wrap without clipping.
Voice.rejectIf: The label is hidden or replaced by an icon.

Frame.decision: Use Frame for box size, radius, row spacing, and layout fit.
Frame.behavior: Frame keeps the control fixed while text uses remaining space.
Frame.example: Permission rows stack on phone and align in desktop tables.
Frame.test: Verify no overflow in narrow and wide containers.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only for surrounding surfaces, not for checkbox state.
Depth.behavior: Depth does not replace focus or selection.
Depth.example: A permission panel can have surface depth while the checkbox stays flat.
Depth.test: Verify selection is clear without shadow.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum for hover, focus, and indicator transitions.
Momentum.behavior: Motion confirms state change without delaying the toggle.
Momentum.example: The check indicator appears quickly after selection.
Momentum.test: Verify reduced-motion and quick state feedback.
Momentum.rejectIf: Motion hides value or blocks interaction.

State.decision: Use State for disabled, error, focus, indeterminate, checked, and unchecked precedence.
State.behavior: State precedence decides visuals and interaction.
State.example: Disabled beats checked; error beats focus.
State.test: Verify precedence across all documented states.
State.rejectIf: State is visual only or contradictory.

Tone.decision: Use Tone for direct, outcome-based labels.
Tone.example: Use 'Enable fuel card' instead of vague consent text.
Tone.test: Verify labels describe outcomes and support text explains risk.
Tone.rejectIf: Copy is ambiguous or legal meaning is guessed.

Growth.decision: Use Growth for reusable selection behavior across settings, filters, and tables.
Growth.behavior: Growth keeps API and states portable as groups scale.
Growth.example: The same contract supports single permission rows and select-all rows.
Growth.test: Verify single and aggregate selection share one state model.
Growth.rejectIf: A product forks checkbox behavior for one screen.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol for check and remove meaning only.
Symbol.behavior: Symbols communicate selected and mixed states.
Symbol.example: Remove symbol means partial selection, not delete.
Symbol.test: Verify symbols match checked and mixed semantics.
Symbol.rejectIf: A decorative icon is placed inside the box.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography for indicator size, weight, fill, and color inheritance.
Iconography.behavior: Icons inherit component state and remain legible.
Iconography.example: Check and remove icons use the same size across densities.
Iconography.test: Verify icon size and fill are tokenized.
Iconography.rejectIf: Icons bypass tokens or change meaning.

Accessibility.decision: Use Accessibility for labels, keyboard, mixed state, focus, errors, and disabled behavior.
Accessibility.behavior: Accessibility makes the boolean value machine-readable.
Accessibility.example: Select-all rows expose mixed state when some children are selected.
Accessibility.test: Verify label, Space toggle, aria-checked mixed, focus, and error association.
Accessibility.rejectIf: The component cannot be operated or understood without sight.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Blocks interaction and explains through support text when possible.

props.name: required
props.notes: Marks a required consent or setting.

productExamples.example: Enable fuel-card permissions for a driver.
Select one driver row or show partial select-all state.
Toggle notification, policy, and permission settings.

do: Use indeterminate only for partial aggregate selection.
dont: Do not use for mutually exclusive choices.
Do not hide consent or policy meaning.
Do not style mixed as checked.
info: Checkbox Group becomes a pattern when choices need grouping, select-all orchestration, or validation across rows.

contextDensityStrategy.layout: full-width rows with clear touch space
stacked settings and compact table rows
readable permission lists and remote-focus surfaces

agentInstructions: Use Checkbox only for boolean or partial boolean choices.
Ask before creating consent, compliance, or money-affecting choices.
Do not use Checkbox when one option must be chosen from a set; use Radio or Select.
rejectIf: Indeterminate is styled as checked without mixed semantics.
Disabled removes contrast below accessibility thresholds.
A group of mutually exclusive choices is built with checkboxes.
